reason: The muscle-development messengers are shown meeting target cells and activating muscle genes, so they seem like a starting point for copying those instructions.
expectation: The messengers will direct a group of cells toward using muscle-protein instructions.

alternatives.reason: The supporting-cell messengers also match a current goal, so I could start with that group instead.

effect: The messengers produced cells with RNA copies of muscle-protein instructions; the protein fibres still need to be made.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the copied instructions lead to a new building goal.
reason: Amino acids are protein building blocks, and these cells now have the muscle-protein instructions.
expectation: The cells will use the amino acids and RNA instructions to build pulling proteins.

alternatives.reason: I could start the other RNA goal before building the muscle proteins.

effect: The amino acids and RNA-equipped cells produced muscle cells with protein fibres that can slide to shorten them. The supporting-cell goal remains.
reaction: The picture makes the connection between the proteins and shortening clearer.
reason: The supporting-cell messengers are shown activating support-protein genes in another group of cells.
expectation: The messengers will lead to cells with RNA copies of support-protein instructions.

effect: The supporting-cell messengers produced RNA copies of support-protein instructions, but the fibre network still needs to be built.
reaction: The parallel with the muscle-cell pathway makes the next step clearer.
reason: Amino acids are protein building blocks, as in the muscle-cell combination, and these cells have support-protein instructions.
expectation: The cells will make supporting protein fibres around themselves.

effect: The cells made supporting connective tissue, with protein fibres around them rather than inside them. That completes the chapter and shows a contrast with the muscle cells.
reaction: The contrast between keeping proteins inside cells and releasing them around cells was interesting.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the muscle cells was most worthwhile because the picture connected their protein fibres to shortening.

leastWorthwhile.text: The supporting-cell pathway felt somewhat repetitive after the muscle pathway, although it led to a useful contrast.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the same DNA and building blocks could lead to proteins used inside muscle cells or released around supporting cells.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt especially arbitrary: the messenger pairings were shown in the pictures, and amino acids were named as protein building blocks.

continue.text: I would choose to continue, because seeing how different cells use the same instructions for different jobs makes me curious about how they form larger structures.
